Class ContainerScreenLayers

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.inject.ContainerScreenLayers
@Internal public final class ContainerScreenLayers extends Object
The one owner of frame composition order on a container screen — what MenuKit draws, and where in vanilla's frame it lands. Every MenuKit draw on an AbstractContainerScreen goes through one of the entry points here; nothing else in the library registers a render hook on a container screen.

The layer stack (bottom to top)

#LayerDrawn by
0screen background, container texturevanilla (extractBackground, an earlier stratum)
1vanilla slots: highlight, item, count, durabilityvanilla (extractSlots, up to the first created slot)
2flow panels: chrome + non-slot elements + created-slot framesMenuKit — beforeSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, Slot, int, int) / aboveSlots(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int)
3created slots: the same extractSlot call as layer 1vanilla (extractSlots, the rest of the list)
4modal dim, overlay panelsMenuKit — aboveSlots(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int)
5carried item, cursorvanilla (extractCarriedItem, next stratum)
6tooltipsvanilla (extractTooltip)

Why layers 1 and 3 are one vanilla pass with MenuKit in the middle

Two things have to be true at once. A panel hides exactly what it covers — pixel for pixel, the way paint does: a panel over half a vanilla slot hides half of it, and the slot stays a normal slot underneath (§0058's opacity is about input; visually a panel is simply on top). So panel chrome must draw after the vanilla slots it may cover. And vanilla draws every slot, created ones included, so a created slot's item must draw after the chrome of the panel that hosts it. The one order that satisfies both is vanilla slots, then panels, then created slots — and vanilla's own extractSlots already walks menu.slots in exactly that order, because MenuKit-Containers appends created slots last. So flow panels are drawn from the extractSlot HEAD of the first created slot in the walk (beforeSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, Slot, int, int)); on a menu with no created slots to draw they fall to the end of the slot pass (aboveSlots(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int)), which is the historical "panels above slots" order. Either way a created slot and a vanilla slot go through the identical extractSlot call, which is what keeps them the same thing to every other mod's slot hook.

A hovered created slot gets vanilla's back-highlight re-issued right after the panels (vanilla drew it before the slot pass, under the chrome); the front highlight is drawn by vanilla after the pass and needs nothing.

Why this class exists

Before it, order was an emergent property of injection points: three registries each registered a Screen.addRenderableOnly renderable (which vanilla iterates inside extractContents, before the slot pass), and a fourth hook re-rendered one of them after the slot pass on recipe-book screens only. Panels drew twice per frame on the inventory screen; panel-vs-slot order differed by screen family; and nothing could be layered reliably because there was no defined "last pass". Nobody owned the decision, so it drifted. This class is the module that hides it (Parnas): a change to composition order is a change here and nowhere else.

The injection points

All on AbstractContainerScreen, reached by every container screen family (plain via extractRenderState, recipe-book via AbstractRecipeBookScreen.extractRenderState, creative via its super call): extractContents HEAD (frameStart(AbstractContainerScreen)), extractSlot HEAD (beforeSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, Slot, int, int)), extractContents RETURN (aboveSlots(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int)). The contents points sit outside the leftPos/topPos matrix push; the slot point sits inside it, so beforeSlot(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, Slot, int, int) pops to absolute coordinates around the panel draw. All are before every nextStratum() and before extractTooltip, so cursor and tooltip layering, and same-frame tooltip flushing, are unchanged.

Non-container screens (VanillaScreenPanelRegistry) have no slot pass and keep their renderable; they are a different surface with no layer question.

Internal — the mixin calls in; consumers never do.

      extractSlot HEAD, for every slot vanilla is about to draw. The first created slot of the frame is the layer 1 / layer 3 boundary: draw layer 2 now, before vanilla draws it. Inside vanilla's slot pass the pose is translated by leftPos/topPos; the panels draw in absolute screen coordinates, so the translation is undone around them.

    • aboveSlots

      public static void aboveSlots(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, int mouseX, int mouseY)
      extractContents RETURN — after vanilla's slot pass. Layer 2 if no created slot triggered it (a menu with none to draw), then layer 4: the modal dim (covers vanilla content AND every flow panel) and overlay panels on top of it. Finally the end-of-frame park: a created slot that no panel presented this frame goes off-screen, so vanilla neither draws nor hit-tests it at a stale position next frame.
